diameterInterpretation: Convex light-curve reconstruction with approximate thermal size: 90.13 km effective diameter (catalog ±1.22 km; additional shape and thermal-model uncertainty). Thermal size supplies a volume-scale approximation. The grid marks unavailable imagery; rotational phase is illustrative.

calibration.uncertaintyKind: Formal catalog uncertainty; excludes extra shape, spin and thermal-model systematics. It is not the total uncertainty of displayed physical scale.
calibration.additionalSystematics: Usui 2011 section 2.3 omits unquantified shape, spin and thermal-model effects. Rotation can add a few to about 10% in size, especially for few detections; no invented total error bar is assigned.
calibration.diameterSemantics: Mean fitted diameter of a nonrotating sphere in the modified Standard Thermal Model. Assigning it as the volume-equivalent diameter of a separate DAMIT mesh is an explicit display-scale approximation, not a published mesh-volume calibration.
calibration.limitations: Hanuš 2021 ASAS-SN study lists 349 measurements and two poles. Select 6039 as the first archived convex solution; the mirror 6040 remains scientifically allowed. ASAS-SN photometry constrains broad shape and spin, not resolved terrain. The thermal scale is approximate. Convex inversion supplies broad outline without resolved craters, concavities, reflectance or regolith texture.
